subject: new web site w. new logo and color scheme

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: new web site w. new logo and color scheme
parts:
Has anyone other than me and Michael had a chance to
check out Michael's new web site design? It's in
the stan-web repo on the new_logo branch.

It features the new logo. I modified the style a wee
bit from where Michael had it to make the h2 headers
darker and to extend the width of the header.

What I'd really like to figure out is how to set it
up so the nav and logo were on the left. The advantage
of the right is that it doesn't disrupt reading the current
page --- the advantage of the left is that it doesn't float
off screen or get too far away.

There's also the issue of whether we release the new logo now
or wait for Stan 3.

Michael also set up a UK-based Stan store for swag, which
would be nice to link into the web site Shop page. Which
brings up the question of whether we should remove the original
logo t-shirts or leave them there for nostalgia sake? Maybe
if we pixelize or distress them to make them look even more retro
so people can wear them ironically?

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] new web site w. new logo and color scheme
parts:
Thanks for checking multiple browsers.

I readjusted so that it works under Firefox.

What do you mean by "not responsive"? You mean you
don't get the background switch in color on the "buttons"
or underlining on the links?

We haven't tried bootstrap. I don't really know anything
about it. It says "mobile first", which isn't really our
target audience for desktop software, though it'd be nice if
it looked good on mobile devices.

But even bootstrap's home page is a mess of scrolling, which
we've tried to avoid. It also looks fairly complicated judging
from the gazillion things on their getting started page:

http://getbootstrap.com/getting-started/

Have you used it? Could you help us get started?
Does it require something server side or does it generate
static HTML?

- Bob

Was the intent when I make it bigger that the image goes away?
And by bigger, I mean zoom (command-shift-+) bigger.

Or did you just mean resizing the window, not the content?
I like how resizing the window shifts from a horizontal to
a vertical layout.

Nobody seems to make safely zoomable pages any more --- they
all want to assume a really fat window on a desktop, whereas I
like to keep my web browser windows narrow. Even GitHub requires
a really wide browser window to see all the nav.
> (agreed re: scrolling. no need for any of that.)

Neither your page nor the Stan home page fit on a window without
scrolling on my Macbookp, even if the web browser extends unzoomed
from top to bottom of screen. We tried, but the content just kept
growing.

- Bob

messages.author: 453ddfeccaf29bbb
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] new web site w. new logo and color scheme
parts:
> Was the intent when I make it bigger that the image goes away?
> And by bigger, I mean zoom (command-shift-+) bigger.

i believe resizing the window and zooming in are equivalent
in bootstrap. i could be mistaken though... there might be
a way to specify different behaviors.

> Or did you just mean resizing the window, not the content?
> I like how resizing the window shifts from a horizontal to
> a vertical layout.

the idea is that on a phone, you get the super simple, vertical
layout. on a tablet you get the intermediate format. on a small
desktop you get appropriately scaled font sizes and on a big
desktop you get bigger fonts.

> Neither your page nor the Stan home page fit on a window without
> scrolling on my Macbookp, even if the web browser extends unzoomed
> from top to bottom of screen. We tried, but the content just kept
> growing.

i'm not against scrolling. i'm just not a huge fan of websites
like: http://www.zensorium.com/tinke/#buy unless the product
is extremely simple and everything can indeed fit in a single page.

cheers
alp
